text:
maya: Heads-up — after landing partial-int8 canary on canary-3 the p95 token latency jumped ~22% for web-search workload. Not steady regressions but spikes correlated with KV cache churn.

sam: hmm, do we have a recent layer sensitivity map? last time embed/lm_head exclusion fixed the worst regressions.

li: Perf alert I pulled from profiler: many cold kernel loads during long context requests; kernel selector bouncing between int4 and fp8 per-layer causing GPU context switches.

anya: sharing quick flame / kernel timeline dump from canary-3 (snip):
```
KERNEL SELECTOR: layer 0..3 -> INT8_kernel_v3
layer 4..7 -> FP8_kernel_v2
layer 8 -> INT8_kernel_v2
KV CACHE HITS: 80% overall but 12% miss bursts at tail
GPU LOAD: kernel swap stalls 8-12ms spikes every ~3rd request
```

maya: perf-bot also posted regression alert:
- baseline (fp8-only): p95 = 38ms
- canary-int8-mix: p95 = 46.4ms (+22%)
- CPU overhead for kernel selection + serialization up ~10%

perf-bot: regression-details: {"metric":"p95_token_latency","delta":"+22%","build":"canary-3-int8-mix"} (automated)

sam: I'm guessing the batching heuristic is grouping heterogeneous requests which forces repeated kernel swaps. Two quick mitigations: 1) pin embed/lm_head to FP8/FP16; 2) bias the batcher to prefer same-kernel affinity for a short window.

li: Agree. Also noticed per-layer calibration variance: some mid layers have huge quantization error if calibrated with short prompts. We should apply layerwise calibration sets (long-context samples) before enabling int8 on those layers.

anya: Proposed config patch for runtime to test today:
```json
{
  "partial_quant": {
    "exclude_patterns": ["embedding","lm_head"],
    "layer_overrides": {
      "layers.4-7": "fp8",
      "layers.10": "fp8-sensitive"
    },
    "batcher": {
      "kernel_affinity_window_ms": 12,
      "prefer_homogeneous_batches": true
    }
  }
}
```

maya: +1 to testing that. Can we also add a short-lived KV cache warmup (preload prefixes) to reduce miss bursts? The misses line up with first tokens after prompt boundaries.

dave: For sensitive layers I'm in favor of a graded fallback policy: quantize for throughput but fall back to fp8 if layer calibration score > threshold or if KV miss rate > X%. We already have hooks for per-layer fallback in kernel selector.

li: I'll run a sensitivity scan with longer contexts and push a new calibration snapshot to S3: s3://redwood-calib/canary-1999001111/scan-2026-03-18.tar.gz. Will also produce a small per-layer error CSV.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: canary-3 -> canary-3a with runtime patch (partial_quant + batcher affinity). ETA 15m.

maya: good. action items: li -> calibration scan + error CSV; anya -> patch + runtime flag; sam -> monitor batcher affinity metrics; dave -> set fallback thresholds. We'll revert if p95 doesn't improve within 2 hours. :thumbsup:

sam: one more note — let's record kernel load counts per-request in tracing so we can quantify 'kernel thrash' before/after. tiny change but will help.

maya: thanks everyone. keeping this thread for results.

(reacts: :eyes: from maya, :rocket: from sam)
